source_text: προσθήσεται ἔναντι Κυρίου διαπαντὸς ἐνώπιον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, διαθήκην αἰώνιον· καὶ ἔσται Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ. Καὶ φάγονται αὐτὰ ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ· ἔστι γὰρ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων τοῦτο αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν θυσιαζομένων τῷ Κυρίῳ, νόμιμον αἰώνιον.» Ἐν δέ γε τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς, ὡς ἕνα πάλιν ἄρτον ἡμῖν τὸν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐξ ἡμῶν· γέγονε γὰρ Θεὸς ὢν φύσει καθ' ἡμᾶς ὁ Λόγος, καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, κατεδείκνυ λέγων πρὸς τὸν ἱεροφάντην Μωϋσέα· «Λάλησον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἐγὼ εἰσάγω ὑμᾶς ἐκεῖ, καὶ ἔσται, ὅταν ἐσθίητε ὑμεῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἄρτων τῆς γῆς, ἀφαιρεῖτε ἀφαίρεμα ἀφόρισμα Κυρίῳ ἀπαρχὴν φυράματος ὑμῶν· ἄρτον ἀφαίρεμα ἀφοριεῖτε αὐτὸ ὡς ἀφαίρεμα ἀπὸ ἅλωνος, οὕτως ἀφαιρήσετε ἀπαρχὴν φυράματος ὑμῶν, καὶ δώσετε τῷ Κυρίῳ ἀφαίρεμα εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν.» Καὶ ἀπονητὶ μὲν διὰ τούτων καταθεῷτό τις ἂν τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας μυστήριον. Λελέξεται δὲ πρὸς ἡμῶν ἐν ἰδίῳ καιρῷ λεπτῶς καὶ ἀπηκριβωμένως, εἰς ἕτερον ἡμῖν ἱδρῶτα συγγραφῆς μετεῤῥηκότος τοῦ λόγου. Πλὴν ἐκεῖνο, οἶμαί που, κατατεθήποι τις ἂν εἴς γε τὸ παρὸν ἡμῖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ ποῖόν τι φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Πολυειδῶς γὰρ ἡμῖν ἐμφανῆ καθιστὰς τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, καὶ δι' ἑτέρου πάλιν αὐτὸν ἀναπλάττει λόγου. Πρὸς γάρ τοι Μωϋσέα φησί· «Καὶ ποιήσεις λυχνίαν ἐκ χρυσίου καθαροῦ, τορνευτὴν ποιήσεις τὴν λυχνίαν· ὁ καυλὸς αὐτῆς καὶ οἱ καλαμίσκοι, καὶ οἱ κρατῆρες, καὶ οἱ σφαιρωτῆρες, καὶ τὰ κρίνα ἐξ αὐτῆς ἔσται. Ἓξ καλαμίσκοι ἐκ τοῦ κλίτους τοῦ δευτέρου.» Καὶ αὖ ἐπὶ τούτοις τὰ εἰς κόσμον τε καὶ χρείαν τῷ τεχνήματι τελοῦντα προστεθεικὼς, κρίνα τέ φημι, καὶ σφαιρωτῆρας καὶ καρυίσκους, ἐπεφώνει πάλιν· «Ὅλη τορνευτὴ, ἐξ ἑνὸς χρυσίου καθαροῦ· καὶ ποιήσεις τοὺς λύχνους αὐτῆς ἑπτὰ, καὶ ἐπιθήσεις τοὺς λύχνους αὐτῆς. Καὶ φανοῦσιν ἐκ τοῦ ἑνὸς προσώπου. Καὶ τὸν ἐπαρυστῆρα αὐτῆς, καὶ τὰ ὑποθέματα αὐτῆς ἐκ χρυσίου καθαροῦ, ποιήσεις πάντα τὰ σκεύη ταῦτα ταλάντου χρυσίου καθαροῦ. Ὅρα, ποιήσεις κατὰ τὸν τύπον τὸν δειχθέντα σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει.» Χρυσῆ μὲν οὖν ἡ λυχνία τύπον ἐπέχουσα τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Φύσει γὰρ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ Θεὸς ὁ Υἱός· χρυσῷ δὲ παρεικαστέον, καθὰ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω διωριζόμεθα, τὴν θείαν λαμπρότητα καὶ ὑπεροχήν. Τορνευτὴ δὲ ὅτι περικαλλὴς καὶ πέρα λόγου παντὸς, τό γε ἧκον εἰς εὐμορφίαν τὴν νοητὴν, ὁ Ἐμμανουήλ. Γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι «Ὡραῖος κάλλει παρὰ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων.» Οὐκοῦν τὸ ἐκτετορνεῦσθαι τὴν λυχνίαν, τὸ εἰς εἶδος ἐκπρεπὲς, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὸ θεοπρεπὲς, κατεδείκνυεν ἂν εὖ μάλα τοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ. Εἰς δεξιὸν δὲ καὶ εὐώνυμον, οἷάπερ ἐκ δένδρου καλαμίσκους ἐκπεφυκότας, συναναθρώσκειν δὲ τῷ μέσῳ καυλῷ, καὶ εἰς ὕψος αἴρεσθαί φησι τὸ ἰσοστατοῦν. Εἷς γὰρ ὢν κατὰ φύσιν ὁ Μονογενὴς, καὶ ἐν ἁπλότητι τῇ κατ' οὐσίαν, ὡς Θεὸς, διαφόροις ἐνεργείαις πολλοστὸς εἶναι δοκεῖ, ἀλλ' οὐδὲν εἰσκεκριμένον ἢ ὀθνεῖον
pass_a_gloss: [Lev 24:8–9 cont.] prosthēsetai it shall be set (lit. added) before the Lord diapantos continually before the sons of Israel, diathēkēn aiōnion an everlasting covenant; and it shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat them en topō hagiō in a holy place; for this is Hagia tōn hagiōn holy of holies for them, and from tōn thysiazomenōn the things sacrificed to the Lord, nomimon aiōnion an everlasting statute. In Numbers, hōs hena palin arton as again one bread ton ex ouranou kai ex hēmōn the one from heaven and from us — for gegone Theos ōn physei kath' hēmas ho Logos the Word, being God by nature, became as we are, kai eskēnōsen en hēmin and tabernacled among us — katedeikny he showed, saying to ton hierophantēn Mōysea Moses the hierophant (revealer of sacred rites): 'Speak to the sons of Israel ... when you go into the land into which I bring you, when you eat from the bread of the land, aphaireite aphairema you shall take off a portion-taken, aphorisma a thing set apart, for the Lord, aparchēn phyramatos firstfruit of your dough; arton aphairema a loaf as portion aphorieite you shall set apart; as aphairema apo halōnos a portion from the threshing floor, so you shall take off the firstfruit of your dough and give to the Lord a portion eis tas geneas for your generations.' aponēti without toil through these one could katatheōto behold to tēs alētheias mystērion the mystery of the truth. Lelexetai it will be said by us en idiō kairō in its own time leptōs finely kai apēkribōmenōs and exactly, meterrēkotos tou logou the discourse having flowed over eis heteron hidrōta syngraphēs into another sweat (labour) of composition. Yet that, I suppose, katatethēpoi one would be amazed at for the present, O Palladius. PALL.: To poion ti phēs; what sort of thing do you say? CYR.: Polyeidōs in many forms emphanē kathistas making manifest ton Emmanouēl Emmanuel, also through another logou account anaplattei he moulds him again. For to Moses he says: 'And you shall make lychnian a lampstand of pure gold; torneutēn turned (finely wrought) you shall make the lampstand; ho kaulos its shaft kai hoi kalamiskoi and branches kai hoi kratēres and cups kai hoi sphairōtēres and knobs kai ta krina and lilies shall be ex autēs out of it. Six branches ek tou klitous tou deuterou from the second side.' And having added the things eis kosmon te kai chreian for ornament and use of the technēmati work — lilies, knobs and karyiskous nut (almond) ornaments — epephōnei he declared again: 'holē torneutē all turned, from one pure gold; and you shall make its lamps seven, and set its lamps, and phanousin ek tou henos prosōpou they shall shine from the one face (front). And ton eparystēra its oil-pourer and ta hypothemata its stands of pure gold; you shall make all these vessels talantou of a talent of pure gold. Hora see, you shall make kata ton typon according to the pattern shown you in the mountain.' Golden then is the lampstand, typon epechousa holding the type of Christ. For physei kai alētheia Theos ho Hyios by nature and truth the Son is God; to gold pareikasteon must be likened, as we determined above, tēn theian lamprotēta kai hyperochēn the divine splendour and preeminence. Turned, because perikallēs very beautiful kai pera logou pantos and beyond all speech, as regards eumorphian tēn noētēn intelligible comeliness, is Emmanuel. For it is written: 'Hōraios kallei fair in beauty beyond the sons of men.' So to ektetorneusthai the being-turned of the lampstand would show to eis eidos ekprepes the excellence of form — clearly to theoprepes the God-befitting — of Emmanuel. To right and left, as from a tree, kalamiskous ekpephykotas branches grown out, he says, synanathrōskein spring up with the middle shaft, and airesthai be raised to height to isostatoun at equal level. For being heis kata physin one by nature, ho Monogenēs the Only-begotten, kai en haplotēti tē kat' ousian and in simplicity as to essence, as God, diaphorois energeiais in various operations pollostos einai dokei seems to be manifold, but nothing eiskekrimenon introduced or othneion alien [cont. §11]
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [Lev 24:8–9 cont.] προσθήσεται it shall be set (lit. added) before the Lord διαπαντός continually before the sons of Israel, διαθήκην αἰώνιον an everlasting covenant; and it shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat them ἐν τόπῳ ἁγίῳ in a holy place; for this is Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων holy of holies for them, and from τῶν θυσιαζομένων the things sacrificed to the Lord, νόμιμον αἰώνιον an everlasting statute. In Numbers, ὡς ἕνα πάλιν ἄρτον as again one bread τὸν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐξ ἡμῶν the one from heaven and from us — for γέγονε Θεὸς ὢν φύσει καθ' ἡμᾶς ὁ Λόγος the Word, being God by nature, became as we are, καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν and tabernacled among us — κατεδείκνυ he showed, saying to τὸν ἱεροφάντην Μωϋσέα Moses the hierophant (revealer of sacred rites): 'Speak to the sons of Israel ... when you go into the land into which I bring you, when you eat from the bread of the land, ἀφαιρεῖτε ἀφαίρεμα you shall take off a portion-taken, ἀφόρισμα a thing set apart, for the Lord, ἀπαρχὴν φυράματος firstfruit of your dough; ἄρτον ἀφαίρεμα a loaf as portion ἀφοριεῖτε you shall set apart; as ἀφαίρεμα ἀπὸ ἅλωνος a portion from the threshing floor, so you shall take off the firstfruit of your dough and give to the Lord a portion εἰς τὰς γενεάς for your generations.' ἀπονητί without toil through these one could καταθεῷτο behold τὸ τῆς ἀληθείας μυστήριον the mystery of the truth. Λελέξεται it will be said by us ἐν ἰδίῳ καιρῷ in its own time λεπτῶς finely καὶ ἀπηκριβωμένως and exactly, μετερρηκότος τοῦ λόγου the discourse having flowed over εἰς ἕτερον ἱδρῶτα συγγραφῆς into another sweat (labour) of composition. Yet that, I suppose, κατατεθήποι one would be amazed at for the present, O Palladius. PALL.: Τὸ ποῖόν τι φής; what sort of thing do you say? CYR.: Πολυειδῶς in many forms ἐμφανῆ καθιστάς making manifest τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ Emmanuel, also through another λόγου account ἀναπλάττει he moulds him again. For to Moses he says: 'And you shall make λυχνίαν a lampstand of pure gold; τορνευτήν turned (finely wrought) you shall make the lampstand; ὁ καυλός its shaft καὶ οἱ καλαμίσκοι and branches καὶ οἱ κρατῆρες and cups καὶ οἱ σφαιρωτῆρες and knobs καὶ τὰ κρίνα and lilies shall be ἐξ αὐτῆς out of it. Six branches ἐκ τοῦ κλίτους τοῦ δευτέρου from the second side.' And having added the things εἰς κόσμον τε καὶ χρείαν for ornament and use of the τεχνήματι work — lilies, knobs and καρυίσκους nut (almond) ornaments — ἐπεφώνει he declared again: 'ὅλη τορνευτή all turned, from one pure gold; and you shall make its lamps seven, and set its lamps, and φανοῦσιν ἐκ τοῦ ἑνὸς προσώπου they shall shine from the one face (front). And τὸν ἐπαρυστῆρα its oil-pourer and τὰ ὑποθέματα its stands of pure gold; you shall make all these vessels ταλάντου of a talent of pure gold. Ὅρα see, you shall make κατὰ τὸν τύπον according to the pattern shown you in the mountain.' Golden then is the lampstand, τύπον ἐπέχουσα holding the type of Christ. For φύσει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ Θεὸς ὁ Υἱός by nature and truth the Son is God; to gold παρεικαστέον must be likened, as we determined above, τὴν θείαν λαμπρότητα καὶ ὑπεροχήν the divine splendour and preeminence. Turned, because περικαλλής very beautiful καὶ πέρα λόγου παντός and beyond all speech, as regards εὐμορφίαν τὴν νοητήν intelligible comeliness, is Emmanuel. For it is written: 'Ὡραῖος κάλλει fair in beauty beyond the sons of men.' So τὸ ἐκτετορνεῦσθαι the being-turned of the lampstand would show τὸ εἰς εἶδος ἐκπρεπές the excellence of form — clearly τὸ θεοπρεπές the God-befitting — of Emmanuel. To right and left, as from a tree, καλαμίσκους ἐκπεφυκότας branches grown out, he says, συναναθρώσκειν spring up with the middle shaft, and αἴρεσθαι be raised to height τὸ ἰσοστατοῦν at equal level. For being εἷς κατὰ φύσιν one by nature, ὁ Μονογενής the Only-begotten, καὶ ἐν ἁπλότητι τῇ κατ' οὐσίαν and in simplicity as to essence, as God, διαφόροις ἐνεργείαις in various operations πολλοστὸς εἶναι δοκεῖ seems to be manifold, but nothing εἰσκεκριμένον introduced or ὀθνεῖον alien [cont. §11]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …it shall be set before the Lord continually, before the sons of Israel, as an everlasting covenant. And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat them in a holy place; for this is most holy for them, from the offerings made to the Lord, a perpetual ordinance’ (Leviticus 24:8–9). In Numbers, again, he showed us the bread that is from heaven and also from us as one bread, for the Word, though God by nature, became like us and dwelt among us (John 1:14). He showed this when he said to Moses, the revealer of sacred rites: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you go into the land into which I am bringing you, then, when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall take off a portion set apart for the Lord, the firstfruits of your dough. You shall set apart a loaf as an offering; as an offering is taken from the threshing floor, so you shall take off the firstfruits of your dough, and you shall give an offering to the Lord throughout your generations’ (Numbers 15:18–21). Through these words one could see the mystery of the truth without effort. It will be discussed by us in detail and with precision at its proper time, when our discourse has passed on to another labor of writing. For the present, though, Palladius, there is one thing, I think, that anyone would marvel at.

Cyril: That in setting Emmanuel before our eyes in many forms, he portrays him once more through yet another passage. For he says to Moses: ‘And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; you shall make the lampstand finely wrought. Its shaft and its branches, its cups, its knobs and its lilies shall be of one piece with it. Six branches from the second side’ (Exodus 25:31–32). Then, after adding the parts that serve the work’s beauty and use, I mean the lilies, the knobs and the almond ornaments (Exodus 25:33–35), he declared again: ‘All of it finely wrought, from one piece of pure gold. And you shall make its seven lamps, and you shall set up its lamps, and they shall shine from the one front. And its oil vessel and its trays you shall make of pure gold; you shall make all these vessels from a talent of pure gold. See that you make them according to the pattern shown you on the mountain’ (Exodus 25:36–40). So the lampstand, which stands as a type of Christ, is of gold. For the Son is God by nature and in truth, and the divine splendor and preeminence must be likened to gold, as we also laid down earlier. It is finely wrought because Emmanuel is beautiful beyond all words in the beauty of form that the mind perceives. For it is written, ‘Fairer in beauty than the sons of men’ (Psalm 45:2). So the finely wrought shape of the lampstand would show Emmanuel’s surpassing beauty of form very well, and plainly this is the beauty that befits God. He says that branches grow out to the right and to the left, as from a tree, and spring up together with the central shaft, rising to an equal height (Exodus 25:32). For the Only-begotten, though he is one by nature and, as God, simple in essence, seems to be many in his various activities; yet there is nothing brought in or foreign…

choices.why: Cyril's text reads προσθήσεται where LXX Leviticus 24:8 has προθήσεται; rendered 'set before' in either case.
LXX has τορευτή (worked in relief); Cyril reads τορνευτή (turned), which he takes as 'beautifully shaped': rendered 'finely wrought' throughout so his argument reads.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation of Leviticus 24:8–9 (the whole quotation is cited as Leviticus 24:5–9 at its start in §9); ends mid-sentence, continued in §11. Cyril's text reads προσθήσεται where LXX Leviticus 24:8 has προθήσεται; rendered 'set before' in either case. Psalm 44:3 LXX = Psalm 45:2 English. Numbers 15:18–21 follows LXX with minor variation (πορεύεσθαι for εἰσπορεύεσθαι). Exodus 25:31–32 is abridged by Cyril ('Six branches from the second side'); rendered as written, not filled out. LXX has τορευτή (worked in relief); Cyril reads τορνευτή (turned), which he takes as 'beautifully shaped': rendered 'finely wrought' throughout so his argument reads. καρυίσκοι (LXX 'nutlets', almond-shaped ornaments) rendered 'almond ornaments'. ἐπαρυστήρ (oil-pourer / lamp filler) rendered 'oil vessel'. ἱεροφάντης rendered 'revealer of sacred rites'. The 'other labor of writing' where Cyril promises to treat Numbers 15 is not named; possibly the Glaphyra on Numbers or a later book of this work (uncertain, no reference given). John 1:14 cited for γέγονε ... καθ' ἡμᾶς ... καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν. 'Exodus 25:32' marks Cyril's paraphrase of the branches; 'rising to an equal height' is his description, not the verse's wording.

changes: ὡς ἕνα ἄρτον: 'showed us the bread from heaven and from us as one bread' (was 'the one bread, as it were')
Πολυειδῶς ... καθιστὰς ... ἀναπλάττει: participle kept subordinate to the main verb; λόγου -> 'passage'
Exodus 25:37 ἐπιθήσεις: 'set up its lamps' (removed added 'on it'; matches §11 and Numbers 8)
'is of gold, since it stands as a type' -> relative clause, removing an added causal link
smoothed the τὸ ἐκτετορνεῦσθαι sentence into natural word order
Scripture checked: Leviticus 24:8-9, Numbers 15:18-21 (starts at 'Speak', v.18), Exodus 25:31-40 split, Psalm 44:3 LXX = Psalm 45:2, John 1:14 all correct
